novelty_flags.label: Comparator promise table / CarpentierKim2015
novelty_flags.one_line: It attributes the single-tail rate and lower bound to “Theorems 3.6 and 3.10,” but the cited Statistica Sinica publication labels the relevant results Theorems 3 and 4; 3.6 is an equation.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 2 (capacity sorting)
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed sorting identity omits the factor m⁻¹ on the selected negative contrasts: for m=2 it gives a survival reduction twice as large as the policy mixture definition permits, and this load-bearing reduction feeds every main theorem.

soundness_flags.label: ass:genuine-survivals
soundness_flags.one_line: Because S_xa is already defined as a conditional survival under positive-probability cells, right-continuity and monotonicity follow from that definition and need not be imposed as a separate class restriction.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The journal article's adaptive rate result is Theorem 3, whose bound is displayed in equation (3.6); its lower bound is Theorem 4. It does not contain Theorems 3.6 and 3.10.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 3.1–3.2, Result 1, and discussion of low overlap
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper learns decisions that reduce tail costs using conformal limits and notes that its limit approaches the maximum outcome support under little or no overlap.
The paper studies constrained treatment-policy learning from efficient causal-effect estimation and establishes asymptotic utilitarian-regret guarantees.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2210.05074, source version for Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work proves a confidence-length impossibility over a local nonparametric tail family and constructs uniformly honest intervals by incorporating worst-case bias.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2209.00246v1, corresponding preprint for the cited JBES article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies continuously valued treatment, fixed treatment pairs, and EQTE/EATE processes over extreme quantile levels with uniform inference.
For bounded outcomes under fixed treated/control counts or random assignment, it finds every treatment rule minimax-regret optimal for its quantile objective.
The paper estimates fixed-level quantile-optimal treatment regimes through successive classification and includes a discrete-outcome smoothing construction.
The paper estimates conditional extreme quantile treatment effects using IPW quantile regression and EVT under a linear conditional quantile model with a common extreme-value-index implication.
